analysis_refs.heading: 2. Scope
analysis_refs.text:
- Free to read: Project Gutenberg (local metadata import), Open Textbook
  Library and the bounded Book Dash catalog (owner-approved source expansion). Other free versions (LibriVox, Wikisource) appear only on detail
  pages as separate items, when a source links them.
- Papers: OpenAlex (when its key and budget are verified), Europe PMC, DOAJ,
  arXiv.
- Children's stories: the reviewed pilot set only, labelled as such.
- The library book page gains an "Also free to read" section.
- Desktop and mobile layouts, all three reading lights.

analysis_refs.heading: Query behavior and operating constraints
analysis_refs.text:
All six retrieval families—GDL, MediaWiki, LoC JSON, Internet Archive search,
LibriVox and Thoth—were probed with a nonsense term. Empty results were observed;
LibriVox expresses this as HTTP 404 with an audiobook-not-found JSON message.
An adapter must distinguish that documented response shape from an outage.
Representative second-page requests were also checked; retain each provider's
paging and scope. These checks are evidence, not implemented app behavior.

analysis_refs.heading: Query behavior and operating constraints
analysis_refs.text:
No paid fallback is proposed. All tested search requests worked anonymously.
Respect current provider limits and use bounded requests, cancellation, backoff
and truthful unavailable states. No numeric unlimited allowance is inferred where
documentation does not publish one. Wikimedia calls should be serial with a
descriptive User-Agent and maxlag for research; Internet Archive also requests
identification of automated clients. LibriVox documents a maximum page size of
500 and pacing for bulk work. We requested only three catalog records at a time,
except GDL's fixed 20-record search page.

analysis_refs.heading: Coverage and the next decision
analysis_refs.text:
If selected to advance later, prioritize GDL for children's coverage, Wikisource
for Indian-language literature, and the five Thoth publishers for shared
engineering. BHL and LoC add historical depth; LibriVox adds audio and requires an
appropriate listening-result design. Keep source qualification and new UI review
before implementation under the agreed workflow.

analysis_refs.heading: C05. Audiobooks and recorded books
analysis_refs.text:
**Best starting points.** [LibriVox API documentation](https://librivox.org/api/info)
describes ID, title, author and genre retrieval, JSON/XML responses and offset
paging. It presently caps `limit` at 500 and asks clients to space bulk requests;
recheck current policies before implementation. Use national-library audio
collections and independently maintained public-domain recording projects for
additional catalogs. [DAISY member organizations](https://daisy.org/about-us/membership/full-members/)
provide accessible-reading leads, with eligibility evaluated individually.

analysis_refs.heading: C05. Audiobooks and recorded books
analysis_refs.text:
**Search process.** Search `"{language}" "public domain audiobooks"`,
`"{institution}" ("talking books" OR audiobooks) (catalog OR API OR RSS)`,
and native-script equivalents for recorded stories/books. Follow a catalog's
producer credits to independently maintained origins. Expand by language/country
and producer type; distinguish library catalogs, volunteer recording projects and
publishers. A LibriVox narrator, recording version or mirror is not a new origin.
Expect a lower qualification rate and document scarcity if 100 independent,
freely accessible catalogs cannot be established.

analysis_refs.heading: Evidence boundaries and next handoff
analysis_refs.text:
Documentation opens succeeded for IBBY, Parag, Book Dash, Gutenberg, OTL, DOAB,
Project Madurai, LibriVox, DAISY and NLS during this planning review. The research
tool returned HTTP 402 for StoryWeaver's open-content page, 502 for NCERT's
textbook page and 403 for DPLA's API page. Sugamya redirected to its current domain
but exposed no readable content to the tool. These observations establish neither
payment requirements nor source-wide outages. No credentials, source accounts,
outreach, bulk harvests or live query qualification probes were performed.

analysis_refs.heading: What the original checks established
analysis_refs.text: Structured responses were obtained from Google Books (using the configured key), Open Library, Internet Archive, DOAJ, OpenAlex, Crossref, arXiv, Europe PMC, CORE, Zenodo, HAL, Wikisource, Library of Congress, and LibriVox. Gutenberg RDF and DOAB record/harvesting responses also worked. OAPEN's OAI service identification worked; a record import was not exercised.

analysis_refs.heading: Behavior
analysis_refs.text:
Ten new integrations are released behind `CONTENT_KNOWLEDGE_ENABLED=true`:
Global Digital Library, LibriVox, Library of Congress digital books, Biodiversity
Heritage Library's Internet Archive collection, African Minds, LSE Press,
Mattering Press, mediastudies.press, punctum books and Python 3.15 documentation.
Five publisher catalogs share Thoth; this is not five separate API infrastructures.
The existing Gutenberg, Open Textbook Library, Book Dash and StoryWeaver snapshots
and the existing OpenAlex/Europe PMC integrations are also selectable. With the
existing production flags, this gives 16 connected sources, not 16 fully audited
origins or complete catalogs.

analysis_refs.heading: Contracts and limits
analysis_refs.text:
- One provider per server request; the browser coordinates the search. No Redis,
  SQL, hosted cache, persisted session or new account/service.
- Fixed-origin adapters bound response size, deadline and paging. Signed cursors
  bind provider, query, types, language, page size and expiry; they work across
  function restarts without storing query results. Changed indexes can change
  pages; exact-key deduplication never merges similar titles or distinct editions.
- The new transport serializes requests per host within an instance, spaces them
  two seconds apart and honors 429 Retry-After. It has no automatic retries.
  This courtesy is not a global request quota across Vercel instances.
- Python's official compressed symbol inventory is bounded and cached for one
  hour in process memory. Search is over symbol/section names, not arbitrary
  full documentation text. Version and same-origin URL checks fail closed.
- GDL uses its public content-search route and published WordPress REST book-ID
  route for exact details. Word-level metadata checks reject substring noise
  such as `Rain` matching only `Shakrain`. Its provider offset advances even when
  inspected rows fail relevance, so filtering does not trap pagination.
- Thoth searches active monographs/edited books in explicit publisher IDs. Exact
  resolution verifies publisher membership and active status. Only canonical
  digital links on reviewed publisher hosts become reading/download actions;
  print, retail and unreviewed mirrors do not.
- LoC requires `access_restricted=false`, digitization and an online resource for
  free access. BHL searches only its biodiversity collection and excludes known
  access-restricted items. Their content rights still vary by item.
- LibriVox is title search and distinct recording identity. Its documented JSON
  404 for no audiobooks is an empty result; other errors remain failures. US
  public-domain statements do not claim worldwide rights.
- Snapshot sources remain labelled incomplete/stale when appropriate. Unknown
  access is hidden by default; an explicit checkbox reveals labelled results with a source record link; no old
  observation is refreshed merely because a user searches it.
- Existing OpenAlex free-allowance and zero-paid-balance checks remain unchanged.
  No key is returned to the browser. No full books/audio are copied.

analysis_refs.heading: Verification and release record
analysis_refs.text:
Hosted preview acceptance, 2026-11-05: all ten new integrations plus OpenAlex
and Europe PMC returned matches and resolved exact native identities (HTTP 200).
WebKit completed real LibriVox search → detail → canonical listening link, then
all-source mathematics (25 results, all 16 sources finished, zero page errors).
Chromium's cloud proxy trust failure was an environment issue; WebKit used the
existing system trust with HTTPS verification intact. No browser trust setting
was changed. Preview account banners reflect its existing configuration.

analysis_refs.heading: Production verification — 2026-11-05
analysis_refs.text: All ten new live query/detail samples and OpenAlex passed in production. Refreshed Gutenberg, OTL and Book Dash query/detail checks passed. StoryWeaver remains stale/unclear and is excluded by the default access filter. Two Europe PMC malaria probes timed out; the UI preserves that source error while other sources return results. This is an unresolved provider/runtime reliability observation, not a zero-result claim. The mobile WebKit all-source query completed all 16 groups with 26 loaded results, no page errors and no horizontal overflow; the LibriVox detail linked to the correct recording. See [saved production evidence](evidence/knowledge-release-2026-11-05/production/deployment.json), including failed probes and screenshots. The temporary preview share link was revoked after testing; protection settings were not weakened.
